'''Dr. Raghunath Anant Mashelkar''' (born 1 January 1943), also known as '''Ramesh Mashelkar''', is an Indian [[chemical engineer]] who is a former Director General of the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR). He was also the President of [[Indian National Science Academy]], President of [[Institution of Chemical Engineers]] (UK) as also the President of [[Global Research Alliance]]. He was also first Chairperson of [[Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research (AcSIR)]]. He is a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]], [[Royal Academy of Engineering|Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering]] (FREng), Foreign Associate of US [[National Academy of Engineering]] and the US [[National Academy of Sciences]].

== Early life and education ==
Raghunath Anant Mashelkar was born on 1 January 1943 in [[Marcel, Goa]] in [[Portuguese India]]. He was brought up in [[Bombay]], [[British India]].{{citation needed|date=February 2025}} Mashelkar is a member of the ''Kalawantin'' community (now known as [[Gomantak Maratha Samaj]] in Goa).<ref name="Review">[http://www.goa-world.com/goa/books/briefrev.htm Goa world book review] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090105185115/http://www.goa-world.com/goa/books/briefrev.htm |date=5 January 2009 }}</ref>

He studied at [[University of Bombay]]'s [[Institute of Chemical Technology|University Department of Chemical Technology]] (UDCT; now the [[Institute of Chemical Technology]], Mumbai) where he obtained [[Bachelor of Engineering|B.Chem Engg]] degree in [[chemical engineering]] in 1966, and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in 1969. He also served as chancellor of the institute during 2014–2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ictmumbai.edu.in/DisplayPage.aspx?page=es&ItemID=e|title=ICT Mumbai|website=www.ictmumbai.edu.in|access-date=2019-06-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190612155521/http://www.ictmumbai.edu.in/DisplayPage.aspx?page=es&ItemID=e|archive-date=12 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Work ==
Raghunath served as the Director General of [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR) - a network of thirty-eight laboratories-for over eleven years. Prior to this, he was Director of [[National Chemical Laboratory]] (NCL) for six years.

He has been a visiting professor at [[Harvard University]](2007–2012), at [[University of Delaware]] (1976, 1988), and at [[Technical University of Denmark]] (1982). He has been Sir Louis Matheson Distinguished Professor at [[Monash University]] for fifteen years (2007–2022).

He has been on the board of directors of several companies such as [[Reliance Industries Limited|Reliance Industries Ltd]], [[Tata Motors]], [[Hindustan Unilever]], [[Thermax]], [[Piramal Group]], [[KPIT Technologies]], etc.

He has been a member of External Research Advisory Board of [[Microsoft]] (USA), Advisory Board of [[VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland|VTT]] (Finland), Corporate Innovation Board of [[Michelin]] (France), Advisory Board of [https://www.nrf.gov.sg/ National Research Foundation (Singapore)], among others.

As Director of India's [[National Chemical Laboratory]] (NCL) during 1989–1995,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ncl-india.org/files/AboutNCL/Organization/PreviousDirectors.aspx|title=National Chemical Laboratory|website=www.ncl-india.org|access-date=2019-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702055310/http://www.ncl-india.org/files/AboutNCL/Organization/PreviousDirectors.aspx|archive-date=2 July 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Mashelkar gave a new orientation to NCL's research programmes with strong emphasis on globally competitive technologies and international patenting. NCL, which was involved only in import substitution research till then, began licensing its patents to multinational companies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.swaminathansivaram.in/media/data/artaicle_global%20chemistry_110515(2).pdf|title=Global Chemistry}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://reflections-shivanand.blogspot.com/2007/08/r-mashelkar-catalyst-for-change.html|title=reflections: R A Mashelkar--Catalyst for Change|last=Kanavi|first=Shivanand|date=8 August 2007|website=reflections|access-date=2019-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190627150346/http://reflections-shivanand.blogspot.com/2007/08/r-mashelkar-catalyst-for-change.html|archive-date=27 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

As Director General of CSIR, Mashelkar led the process of transformation of CSIR. The book 'World Class in India', has ranked CSIR among the top twelve organizations, who have managed the radical change the best in post-liberalised India.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://penguin.co.in/book/business/world-class-india/|title=World Class in India|website=Penguin India|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190627150348/https://penguin.co.in/book/business/world-class-india/|archive-date=27 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

The process of CSIR transformation has been heralded as one of the ten most significant achievements of Indian Science and Technology in the twentieth century, by eminent astrophysicist Prof. [[Jayant Narlikar]], in his book, [https://penguin.co.in/book/non-fiction/the-scientific-edge/ The Scientific Edge].

Mashelkar campaigned strongly with Indian academics, researchers and corporates for strengthening the IPR ecosystem. Under his leadership, CSIR occupied the first position in [[World Intellectual Property Organization|WIPO]]'s top fifty [[Patent Cooperation Treaty|PCT]] filler among all the developing nations in 2002. CSIR progressed in US patent filing to an extent that they reached 40% share of the US patents granted to India in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iisc.ernet.in/currsci/sep102003/570.pdf|title=Innovation chain and CSIR}}</ref>

Led by Mashelkar, CSIR successfully fought the battle of revocation of the US patent on wound healing properties of ''turmeric (USP 5,401,5041)'' claiming that this was India's traditional knowledge and therefore not novel.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jayaraman|first=K. S.|date=1 September 1997|title=US patent office withdraws patent on Indian herb|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=389|issue=6646|page=6|doi=10.1038/37838|pmid=9288953|issn=1476-4687|bibcode=1997Natur.389R...6J|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Horowitz-Ghazi |first1=Alexi |last2=Messick |first2=Molly |last3=Rubin |first3=Willa |last4=Beras |first4=Erika |title=How one man fought a patent war over turmeric |url=https://www.npr.org/2023/09/01/1197321273/turmeric-india-biopiracy-patent-tkdl |access-date=1 December 2023 |work=[[Planet Money]] |publisher=[[NPR]] |date=September 1, 2023}}</ref> Mashelkar also chaired the Technical Committee, which successfully challenged<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=http://www.mondaq.com/india/x/586384/Patent/Traditional+Knowledge+And+Patent+Issues+An+Overview+Of+Turmeric+Basmati+Neem+Cases|title=Traditional Knowledge And Patent Issues: An Overview of Turmeric, Basmati, Neem Cases. - Intellectual Property - India|website=www.mondaq.com|access-date=2019-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190627150348/http://www.mondaq.com/india/x/586384/Patent/Traditional%2BKnowledge%2BAnd%2BPatent%2BIssues%2BAn%2BOverview%2BOf%2BTurmeric%2BBasmati%2BNeem%2BCases|archive-date=27 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> the US patents on Basmati Rice (USP 5,663,484) by RiceTec Company, Texas, (2001). This opened up new paradigms in the protection of traditional knowledge with WIPO bringing in a new internal patent classification system, where sub-groups on traditional knowledge were created for the first time. This led to the creation of India's [[Traditional Knowledge Digital Library]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/council-scientific-industrial-research-csir/csir-unit|title=CSIR-UNIT: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL), New Delhi {{!}} India Science, Technology & Innovation|website=www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in|access-date=2019-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190707163153/http://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/council-scientific-industrial-research-csir/csir-unit|archive-date=7 July 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> which helped in prevention of the grant of wrong patents on traditional knowledge.

He pioneered the concept of ''"Gandhian Engineering"''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gyti.techpedia.in/news-detail/6|title=Gandhian Engineering: How It Can Change the World 80 {{!}} Gandhian Young Technological Innovation Award|website=gyti.techpedia.in|access-date=2019-06-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170926170133/http://gyti.techpedia.in/news-detail/6|archive-date=26 September 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> in 2008 (Getting More from Less for More People). His paper with late [[C. K. Prahalad|C.K. Prahalad]] titled '[https://hbr.org/2010/07/innovations-holy-grail Innovation's Holy Grail]' has been considered as a significant contribution to inclusive innovation. His other contributions amplify the concept of More from Less for More.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/CountryNews/9368_KR_NARAYANAN_ORATION.pdf|title=2018 K.R. Narayanan Oration: Dismantling Inequality through ASSURED Innovation|access-date=27 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190627150349/https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/CountryNews/9368_KR_NARAYANAN_ORATION.pdf|archive-date=27 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://penguin.co.in/book/business/leapfrogging-to-pole-vaulting/|title=Leapfrogging to Pole-vaulting|website=Penguin India|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190627150347/https://penguin.co.in/book/business/leapfrogging-to-pole-vaulting/|archive-date=27 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

He was on the Engineering and Computer Science jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] from 2009 to 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Foundation|first=Infosys Science|date=30 December 2020|title=Infosys Prize - Jury 2015|url=https://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/jury/jury-2015.asp#Engineering-and-Computer-Science|access-date=30 December 2020}}</ref>

He has been a jury member of the Prestigious [[Queen Elizabeth Prize]] for Engineering since 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://qeprize.org/news/meet-new-qeprize-judges-raghunath-mashelkar |title=Meet the new QEPrize judges: Raghunath Mashelkar }}</ref>

== National contributions ==
Mashelkar was a member of the Scientific Advisory Council to the Prime Minister and also of the [https://web.archive.org/web/20070612040949/http://psa.gov.in/uniquepages/singlepage_new.asp?ID=4 Scientific Advisory Committee to the Cabinet] set up by successive governments. He has chaired sixteen high powered committees set up to look into diverse issues ranging from national auto fuel policy<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pib.nic.in/archieve/lreleng/lyr2003/roct2003/06102003/r0610200313.html|title=PIB Press Releases|access-date=21 June 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040310000323/http://pib.nic.in/archieve/lreleng/lyr2003/roct2003/06102003/r0610200313.html|archive-date=10 March 2004|url-status=live}}</ref> to overhauling the Indian drug regulatory system & dealing with the menace of spurious drugs.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://cdsco.nic.in/html/Final%20Report%20mashelkar.pdf |title=A Comprehensive Examination of Drug Regulatory Issues, including the Problem of Spurious Drugs |access-date=21 June 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110915200625/http://cdsco.nic.in/html/Final%20Report%20mashelkar.pdf |archive-date=15 September 2011 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was appointed by the Government as Assessor for the One-man Inquiry Commission investigating into the Bhopal Gas Tragedy (1985–86), and as Chairman of the committee for investigating the Maharashtra Gas Cracker Complex accident (1990–91).<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.100385|title=Csir News Vol.45, No. 1-22(jan-nov)1995|last=Not Available|date=1995}}</ref>

Deeply connected with the innovation movement in India, Mashelkar served as the Chairman of India's National Innovation Foundation (2000–2018). He chaired Reliance Innovation Council,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ril.com/Innovation-R-D/Innovation.aspx|title=Reliance Innovation Council India - Raghunath Mashelkar {{!}} Mukesh Ambani {{!}} Jean-Marie Lehn {{!}} Robert Grubbs {{!}} George Whitesides {{!}} Gary Hamel {{!}} William Haseltine|website=www.ril.com|access-date=2019-06-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626153405/https://www.ril.com/Innovation-R-D/Innovation.aspx|archive-date=26 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> KPIT Technologies Innovation Council, Persistent Systems Innovation Council and [[Marico]] Foundation's Governing Council.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maricoinnovationfoundation.org/|title=HOME|website=Marico Foundation|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190529230305/https://www.maricoinnovationfoundation.org/|archive-date=29 May 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> He co-chairs the [[Maharashtra State Innovation Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.msins.in/#!/organization-structure|title=Maharashtra State Innovation Society - General Body|access-date=26 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626153409/https://www.msins.in/#!/organization-structure|archive-date=26 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Research ==

Mashelkar has made contributions in [[transport phenomena]], in [[thermodynamics]] of swelling, superswelling and shrinking [[polymer]]s, modelling of [[Polymerization|polymerisation]] reactors, and engineering analysis of [[Non Newtonian fluid|Non-Newtonian]] flows.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mashelkar.com/work/research-papers|title=Research Papers|access-date=10 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611064243/http://www.mashelkar.com/work/research-papers|archive-date=11 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Controversy ==

In 2005, the Indian government established a technical expert group on patent laws under the chairmanship of Mashelkar. Its purpose was to determine whether amendments made in Indian patent law were [[TRIPS]] compliant. The committee unanimously concluded that the amendments were not [[TRIPS]] compliant.

The report generated controversy when editorials published simultaneously in the ''[[Times of India]]''<ref name="TOI 2007-02-22">{{cite news|last=Mitta|first=Manoj|title=Mashelkar takes back report after plagiarism row|work=[[The Times of India]]|date=22 February 2007|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Mashelkar-takes-back-report-after-plagiarism-row/articleshow/1653926.cms|access-date=12 June 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016232156/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2007-02-22/india/27871784_1_technical-inaccuracies-mashelkar-scientific-and-industrial-research|archive-date=16 October 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> and ''[[The Hindu]]''<ref name="TH 2007-02-12">{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-opinion/First-attempt-to-dent-a-compromised-patent-system/article14719338.ece|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420142359/https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-opinion/First-attempt-to-dent-a-compromised-patent-system/article14719338.ece|url-status=live|archive-date=20 April 2021|title=First attempt to dent a compromised patent system|last=Park|first=Chan|date=12 February 2007|work=[[The Hindu]]|author2=Achal Prabhala|url-access=subscription|access-date=12 June 2007}}</ref> alleged parts of the report had been plagiarised. Mashelkar subsequently withdrew the report due to the alleged plagiarism,<ref name="IE 2007-02-22" /> admitting to flaws in the report<ref name="TOI 2007-02-22" /><ref name="TH 2007-02-22">{{cite news|last=Sharma|first=Ravi|author2=Sara Hiddleston|title=Mashelkar committee on Patent Law withdraws report; seeks more time|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=22 February 2007|url=http://www.hindu.com/2007/02/22/stories/2007022206751200.htm|access-date=18 June 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930232135/http://www.hindu.com/2007/02/22/stories/2007022206751200.htm|archive-date=30 September 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> whilst stating, "This is the first time such a thing has happened."<ref name="IE 2007-02-22">{{cite news|last=Bagla|first=Pallava|title='Plagiarism' in his panel's report, Mashelkar tells Govt to withdraw it|work=[[The Indian Express]]|date=22 February 2007|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/story/23941.html|access-date=18 June 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070403024333/http://www.indianexpress.com/story/23941.html|archive-date=3 April 2007|url-status=live}}</ref> He later also explained that the technical flaw was not the alleged lack of attribution but it was citing the attribution at the end of the report than in the body of the report due to the style adopted for the report.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Politics/7uDji9nz9vWO3n1dJ3gzUI/Theres-a-lesson-to-be-learnt-here-says-Mashelkar.html|title=There's a lesson to be learnt here, says Mashelkar|last=Koshy|first=Bhuma Shrivastava and Jacob P.|date=26 February 2007|website=Mint|language=en|access-date=2019-06-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626153337/https://www.livemint.com/Politics/7uDji9nz9vWO3n1dJ3gzUI/Theres-a-lesson-to-be-learnt-here-says-Mashelkar.html|archive-date=26 June 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

The controversy was raised in the [[Indian Parliament]], with demands that the report be "trashed" and the issues be referred to a joint standing committee.<ref name="CPI-M 2007-02-22">{{cite news|title=Trash Mashelkar panel report on patent law: CPI-M|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=22 February 2007|url=http://www.hindu.com/thehindu/holnus/002200702221340.htm|access-date=20 June 2007 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070930201535/http://www.hindu.com/thehindu/holnus/002200702221340.htm <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 30 September 2007}}</ref><ref name="TH 2007-03-05">{{cite news|title=Scrap Mashelkar report|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=5 March 2007|url=http://www.hindu.com/2007/03/05/stories/2007030505351300.htm|access-date=20 June 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071001062511/http://www.hindu.com/2007/03/05/stories/2007030505351300.htm|archive-date=1 October 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, the government instead referred the report back to the technical expert group to reexamine and correct the inaccuracies. The report was resubmitted after corrections in March 2009 and was accepted by the Government as such.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tapanray.in/the-government-of-india-accepts-the-mashelkar-committee-report-on-incremental-innovation-what-does-it-really-mean/|title=The Government of India accepts the Mashelkar Committee Report on 'Incremental Innovation' – what does it really mean? {{!}} PILMAN|website=www.tapanray.in|date=20 August 2009 |language=en-US|access-date=2018-07-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180731183322/http://www.tapanray.in/the-government-of-india-accepts-the-mashelkar-committee-report-on-incremental-innovation-what-does-it-really-mean/|archive-date=31 July 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/P4pUZLxGSXlCFai4xYNtmI/RA-Mashelkar--For-me-it8217s-national-interest-that-com.html|title=RA Mashelkar {{!}} For me, it's national interest that comes first - Livemint|website=www.livemint.com|access-date=2018-07-31|date=21 October 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180731183554/https://www.livemint.com/Companies/P4pUZLxGSXlCFai4xYNtmI/RA-Mashelkar--For-me-it8217s-national-interest-that-com.html|archive-date=31 July 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
[[File:The President, Shri Pranab Mukherjee presenting the Padma Vibhushan Award to Dr. Raghunath Anant Mashelkar, at a Civil Investiture Ceremony, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on March 31, 2014.jpg|thumb|The President, Shri Pranab Mukherjee presenting the Padma Vibhushan Award to Dr. Raghunath Anant Mashelkar, at a Civil Investiture Ceremony, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on March 31, 2014]]

Mashelkar has received several awards and is a member of numerous scientific bodies and committees.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mashelkar.com/about/awards-and-recognitions|title=Awards and Recognitions|work=RAMashelkar|access-date=10 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611091658/http://www.mashelkar.com/about/awards-and-recognitions|archive-date=11 June 2015|url-status=live }}</ref> So far, '''56''' universities from around the world have honored him with honorary doctorates, which include Universities of London, Salford, Pretoria, Wisconsin, Swinburne, Monash, Deakin and Delhi.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mashelkar.com/|title=R A Mashelkar|website=www.mashelkar.com|access-date=2019-06-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611073153/http://www.mashelkar.com/|archive-date=11 June 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>
Academy of Grassroots Studies and Research of India (AGRASRI), Tirupati, awarded him the Rajiv Gandhi Outstanding Leadership National Award for the year 2007 on 20 August 2007 at Tirupati, by Shri R.L.Bhatia, the then Governor of Kerala. Dr. Mashelkar delivered the 6th Rajiv Gandhi Memorial Lecture on 20 August 2007 at Tirupati.
He surpasses the record for the highest number of honorary doctorates awarded to any Indian engineer, which was previously held by Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam with 48 honorary doctorates.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.psa.gov.in/innerPage/psa-initiatives-covid/dr-p-j-abdul-kalam/3808 | title=Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam &#124; Principal Scientific Adviser }}</ref>

'''Honours by President of India: (highest Indian civilian awards)'''

* [[Padma Shri]], India's fourth highest civilian award (1991) 
* [[Padma Bhushan]], India's third highest civilian award (2000) 
* [[Padma Vibhushan]], India's second highest civilian award (2014)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=69364|title=Padma Awards Announced|date=25 January 2014|publisher=Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs|access-date=26 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222101141/http://www.pib.nic.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=102735|archive-date=22 February 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Election to Prestigious Academies (International):'''

== Social service ==
Mashelkar established the [https://mashelkarfoundation.org Anjani Mashelkar Foundation] in 2011 to encourage inclusive innovation which includes the excluded by deploying disruptive high technology, scalable products and services often through breakthrough business models.

The foundation has awarded the Anjani Mashelkar Prize to the best innovators of the country with a motive to recognise and reward such innovators who develop high technology solutions for the excluded members of society. As on 2024, the annual Anjani Mashelkar Prize has been awarded 14 times.
